Find the Cartesian equation of the parabola defined by the parametric equations

$$
x-4=-2{t}^{2},\,y-1=-4t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

feedback.problem:
Consider the following parametric equation of the parabola 

$$
x-3=-{t}^{2},\,y+4=-2t,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

The Cartesian equation of this parabola is

$(y\,+$
{{field-1}}$)^{2}=$
{{field-2}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, let's make $t$ the subject of the parametric equations. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & =-(x-3),\,t=-\frac{y+4}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Squaring both sides of the second equation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & ={(-\frac{y+4}{2})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{(y+4)^{2}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

We can now eliminate the parameter $t$ by substituting the above into the equation ${t}^{2}=-(x-3)$ and rearranging to find the Cartesian equation of the parabola, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{(y+4)^{2}}{4} & =-(x-3) \\ (y+4)^{2} & =-4(x-3) \\ {(y+4)}^{2} & =-4(x-3)\end{aligned}
$$
